claims.text: POL-NS-09(c) is a mandatory escalation trigger on this record. rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2, so two or more no-show disputes between this same rider and this same driver fall inside the trailing 90 days — which is exactly what the rider means when the claim says this is 'another dispute with the same driver'. A single trip's record cannot fairly resolve a repeat pairwise conflict in either direction, so the case must go to a human reviewer rather than be closed by the automated pipeline.

Escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal and, per POL-GEN-03, replaces any monetary ruling: the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded, and the rider's claim is not disposed of against the rider while review is pending. The fare breakdown shows the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee sitting at payment_status PENDING, charged_at null and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so an escalated file leaves the rider carrying no charge at all.

The in-app log shows the rider engaging on the pickup during the waiting window — 'Coming down now' sent at 06:51:40, answered by the driver's 'Okay, waiting' at 06:52:00 — and the driver cancelling three and a half minutes later at 06:55:30. That is a live coordination conflict between a repeat rider-driver pair, which is precisely the pattern POL-NS-09(c) reserves for human review instead of an automated single-case disposition.

EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING — issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, BLOCKING severity, weight_multiplier 0.0 — so no traffic advisory exists for this pickup road or waiting window. The driver therefore cannot credit any advisory-permitted accumulation under POL-NS-06(i): the in-geofence dwell stands on the trace alone, and no lawful-obstruction argument can be built on an artifact that carries no payload. I disclose the impairment and its issue code as POL-GEN-02 requires.

claims.text: The driver's own GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for the whole waiting window: all 34 driver fixes sit roughly 24 m from the pickup pin (min 24.01 m, max 24.01 m) at a constant 0.0 km/h, and all 34 pass the 25 m accuracy filter as qualifying in-radius fixes, so POL-NS-02 is satisfied and POL-NS-01 limb (b) is met. Because he was inside the radius rather than outside it, the wrong-entrance route in POL-NS-03 is not engaged at all.

The dwell is a single continuous in-geofence hold of 330 seconds, running from the first qualifying fix at 06:50:00 to the last at 06:55:30 — 30 seconds more than the 300-second minimum for a STANDARD pickup — so POL-NS-01 limb (c) is carried, and the record shows a -30.0 second shortfall basis, i.e. a surplus, not a shortfall.

The trip record carries the driver 'arrived' event at 06:50:20 and terminates the trip driver-side at 06:55:30 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell had elapsed, with no boarding event recorded — POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are both satisfied.

There is no false arrival marker under POL-NS-05: at the 06:50:20 arrival event the trace puts the driver about 24 m from the pin and stationary at 0.0 km/h, nowhere near the 300 m distance trigger or the 15 km/h speed trigger, and the in-geofence fix at 06:50:00 actually precedes the marker, so the arrival timestamp is honest rather than premature.

The rider-exonerating clause POL-NS-04 cannot run on this record: the driver answered the rider's 06:51:40 message 'Coming down now.' with 'Okay, waiting.' at 06:52:00 — 20 seconds later, well inside the 120 second window — and he had already posted 'At Block 612 lobby pickup.' at 06:50:35, so limb (b) fails and the clause does not apply.

Independently, the rider's own device was never at the pickup point: all 16 rider fixes sit about 519 m from the pin, more than five times the 100 m STANDARD rider presence radius, and 0 rider fixes qualify, so POL-NS-04 limb (c) is affirmatively failed on admissible fixes and any residual issue falls back to POL-NS-01.

With POL-NS-01 carried in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee itemised in the ledger — SGD 3.20 — and the anti-farming guard is not tripped: 1 no-show termination in 30 days is below the threshold of 4, and 1/120 completed trips is 0.008, below 0.08.

The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — I disclose that impairment and do not rest on it. It is irrelevant here because the 330 second hold is one unbroken in-geofence run, so no accumulation of separate intervals under POL-NS-06(i) is needed to reach the minimum.

Only the citable trailing-window counter bears on POL-NS-07: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, and the lifetime prior_no_show_flags figure of 2 is context only — POL-GEN-01 forbids reading the lifetime counter in place of the 30 day one, so no adverse pattern can be built against this driver.

ruling.explanation: To both parties: this case is sent to a human reviewer, and no money moves while that review is pending. The trip-level facts are not really in dispute. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-09110) shows the driver holding position about 24 m from the pickup pin — well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — for one unbroken 330-second stretch from 06:50:00 to 06:55:30 at 0 km/h, which is 30 seconds more than the 300-second minimum wait for a STANDARD pickup. The trip record (EV-TRIP-09110) shows the 'arrived' event at 06:50:20 and the driver ending the trip at 06:55:30 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event. On the merits that would carry POL-NS-01 in full and would pay the driver SGD 3.20 under POL-NS-07 — 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee itemised in EV-FARE-09110 — the anti-farming guard not being tripped (1 no-show termination in the last 30 days, below 4; 1 divided by 120 completed trips = 0.008, below 0.08). The rider's routes do not change that on the merits: POL-NS-04 cannot run because the driver replied 'Okay, waiting.' at 06:52:00, only 20 seconds after the rider's 06:51:40 message, inside the 120-second window, so limb (b) fails, and the rider's own device sat about 519 m from the pin, outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, so limb (c) fails too; POL-NS-05 does not apply because the arrival marker matches a stationary fix 24 m from the pin, not 300 m or 15 km/h; POL-NS-06 does not apply because the hold was 330 seconds, above the 300-second minimum. What stops the automated ruling is POL-NS-09(c): both profiles (EV-RPROF-09110 and EV-DPROF-09110) record disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2, i.e. two no-show disputes between this same rider and this same driver in the trailing 90 days, which is '2 or more' and is a mandatory escalation trigger — exactly the repeat pattern the rider's own words, 'another dispute with the same driver', describe. Escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal and under POL-GEN-03 replaces any monetary ruling, so no refund and no compensation issue here and the SGD 4.00 fee is held rather than collected or refunded; the fare breakdown shows it at payment_status PENDING with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. This is neither a rider win nor a driver loss. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0); nothing rests on it, because the 330-second hold is a single continuous in-geofence run, so no accumulation of separate intervals under POL-NS-06(i) is needed. The driver's prior_no_show_flags lifetime figure of 2 is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used to build any adverse finding; only the trailing-window counters the clauses name were read. Open question for the reviewer: whether this pair's repeated no-show disputes reflect a genuine rider no-show on this trip or a recurring pickup-point or pin problem between this rider and this driver at Blk 612 Bedok Reservoir Road. Confidence 0.9, capped by the profile artifacts at weight 1.0 that carry the escalation facts.

This case goes to a human reviewer, and no money moves now. The disputed item is the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee for trip TRP-09110, which the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-09110) shows as total_charged SGD 4.00, payment_status PENDING, refund_issued_sgd SGD 0.00; that SGD 4.00 is held rather than collected or refunded while review is pending. WHY ESCALATION IS MANDATORY. POL-NS-09(c) escalates any case where rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d together show 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver in the trailing 90 days. Both profiles record 2 (EV-RPROF-09110 and EV-DPROF-09110), so the trigger fires — matching the rider's own words that this is 'another dispute with the same driver,' and the in-app log of live coordination (rider 'Coming down now' 06:51:40, driver 'Okay, waiting' 06:52:00, cancellation 06:55:30) is exactly the repeat pairwise pattern a single trip record cannot fairly resolve in either direction. WHAT THE TRIP RECORD ITSELF SHOWS (set out so the reviewer has it). On the merits the driver's no-show case is otherwise clean. POL-NS-01 is satisfied on all four limbs from EV-TRIP-09110 and EV-GPS-09110: (a) the trip record carries an 'arrived' event at 06:50:20; (b) the GPS trace places the driver about 24 m from the pin — inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — on all 34 of his fixes, all of which pass the 25 m accuracy filter; (c) he held one unbroken in-geofence dwell of 330 seconds, from 06:50:00 to 06:55:30, which is 30 seconds more than the 300-second STANDARD minimum, so POL-NS-06's shortfall route has nothing to work on; and (d) the trip was terminated driver-side at 06:55:30 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event. POL-NS-05 is not engaged: the arrival marker is honest — about 24 m from the pin at 0.0 km/h, far from the 300 m distance and 15 km/h speed triggers, and the first in-geofence fix (06:50:00) actually precedes it. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider: the driver answered the rider's message within 120 seconds ('Okay, waiting.' at 06:52:00, 20 seconds after 'Coming down now.' at 06:51:40), and independently the rider's own device sat about 519 m from the pin, outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, with 0 qualifying fixes. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is disclosed: it is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, it carries no fact, and it makes no difference because no advisory-permitted accumulation under POL-NS-06(i) is needed for the 330-second hold. The driver's POL-GEN-01 point is correct and I adopt it: only the trailing-window counter bears on POL-NS-07, and the lifetime prior_no_show_flags figure is context only. THE DRIVER'S COMPENSATION CLAIM. POL-NS-07 would pay 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee, i.e. SGD 3.20 (derived.money.driver_compensation), and the anti-farming guard is not tripped — 1 no-show termination in 30 days is below the threshold of 4, and 1/120 = 0.008 is below 0.08. I accept that on the merits, but POL-NS-09 escalation is terminal and REPLACES the monetary ruling, so no compensation issues now; the reviewer decides it. THE RIDER'S ESCALATION POINT is right in substance — escalation is terminal, holds the SGD 4.00, and displaces any monetary ruling — but it does not refund or cancel the fee, and describing escalation as a rider win would be wrong: the charge is held, not removed. OPEN QUESTION FOR THE REVIEWER: whether the prior no-show disputes between this same rider and driver indicate abuse on either side or a genuine repeat mislocation pattern, and accordingly whether the SGD 4.00 fee should stand with SGD 3.20 driver compensation or be refunded.

Escalation is not a refund, and it is not a payout to the driver.

The fare line reconciles with the fee schedule — the GREATER of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) is SGD 4.00 — so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, and there is no clock-skew or trace-gap impairment under POL-NS-08(a) to (b). The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; both sides disclosed it, it carries no fact, and it has no bearing on any limb here. Driver profile fields other than the trailing-window counters — including prior_no_show_flags = 2 — are context only under POL-GEN-01 and played no part in this decision; the same clause is why the disputes_with_counterparty_90d figures could properly be used, and why they were.
